description: Synthetic retrieval evaluation set for Team Memory stage 02. Written by hand to resemble engineering team knowledge; not real pilot data. Queries are labeled with the memory keys that answer them; conflicts lists (deeper, ancestor) pairs that a reviewer should see as conflict or override candidates, and hard_negatives lists related same-topic pairs that are not conflicts.

memories.title: Structured JSON logging with zap
memories.content: All Go services log JSON lines with go.uber.org/zap. Every entry carries trace_id and span_id fields. Never log request or response bodies.
memories.rationale: One log format lets the shared pipeline parse every service.

memories.title: Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs
memories.content: Significant technical decisions are written as Architecture Decision Records in docs/adr of the owning repository using the MADR template. Pull requests that implement a decision link the ADR number.

memories.title: Secrets come from Vault
memories.content: Services read credentials from HashiCorp Vault through the vault-agent sidecar. Committing .env files that contain real secrets, API keys or passwords is forbidden; use .env.example with placeholders.
memories.rationale: Leaked keys in repositories caused two incidents in 2024.

memories.title: Personal data stays in the EU
memories.content: Personal data (PII) is stored and processed only in the eu-west-1 region. Exports to analytics systems must be pseudonymized before they leave the production database.
memories.rationale: GDPR data residency commitments in customer contracts.

memories.title: Go services pin Go 1.25
memories.content: Go services declare go 1.25 and a matching toolchain directive in go.mod. Upgrades happen org-wide once a quarter.

memories.title: OpenTelemetry for tracing
memories.content: All services export traces over OTLP to the shared OpenTelemetry collector. Jaeger client libraries are deprecated and must be removed.
memories.rationale: Vendor-neutral instrumentation and one collector to operate.

memories.title: Every user-facing service defines an SLO
memories.content: User-facing services publish an availability SLO (default 99.9% over 28 days) and a p95 latency objective, with an error budget policy that freezes feature work when the budget is spent.

memories.title: On-call is managed in PagerDuty
memories.content: Each team has a PagerDuty schedule named <team>-primary. Incidents escalate to the secondary after 15 minutes without acknowledgement. Page the owning team's primary for production outages.

memories.title: Two approvals for production changes
memories.content: The main branch is protected. Changes need two approving reviews, one from a CODEOWNERS entry for the touched paths, and green CI before merge.

memories.title: Calico over Cilium for cluster networking
memories.content: Kubernetes clusters use Calico as the CNI plugin. Cilium was evaluated and rejected for now; revisit in 2027.
memories.rationale: The platform team already runs BGP peering with Calico and lacked eBPF operating experience.

memories.title: Cloud infrastructure lives in infra-terraform
memories.content: Every cloud resource is defined in the infra-terraform repository. Atlantis posts the plan on each pull request and applies after merge. No console click-ops.

memories.title: Service-to-service traffic uses mTLS
memories.content: Traffic between services inside the cluster is encrypted and authenticated with mutual TLS provided by the Linkerd service mesh.

memories.title: Postmortems are blameless and due in five days
memories.content: After every SEV1 or SEV2 incident the owning team writes a blameless postmortem within five business days and reviews action items at the weekly ops meeting.

memories.title: Feature flags through LaunchDarkly
memories.content: Feature flags are managed in LaunchDarkly. Remove a flag and its code paths within 30 days of a full rollout.

memories.title: Wrap Go errors with context
memories.content: Wrap errors with fmt.Errorf("doing x: %w", err) so callers can use errors.Is and errors.As. Do not use github.com/pkg/errors in new code.

memories.title: Store timestamps in UTC
memories.content: Timestamps are stored as timestamptz and handled in UTC end to end; convert to local time zones only at the presentation layer.

memories.title: Renovate manages dependency updates
memories.content: Renovate opens dependency update pull requests. Patch updates with passing CI auto-merge; minor and major updates need a human review.

memories.title: PostgreSQL 17 is the default datastore
memories.content: Platform services store relational data in PostgreSQL 17 on managed RDS unless an ADR justifies another store.
memories.rationale: ACID transactions and existing team expertise.

memories.title: Database connection pool sizing
memories.content: Platform services size their pgx pool with the DB_POOL_MAX_CONNS environment variable, default 20 connections per pod.

memories.title: Internal APIs use gRPC
memories.content: Internal service APIs are gRPC. Protobuf definitions live in go-commons/proto and are managed with buf; buf breaking runs in CI.

memories.title: Schema migrations with goose
memories.content: Database schema migrations are written for goose, embedded in the binary, and forward-only. Down migrations are not used in production.

memories.title: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter
memories.content: Outbound calls retry with the retryWithJitter helper from go-commons/retry: exponential backoff, full jitter, at most five attempts. Never retry a non-idempotent POST unless it carries an idempotency key.

memories.title: Autoscaling targets for platform deployments
memories.content: Platform deployments use a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) targeting 70% CPU utilization with minReplicas 3.

memories.title: Platform logs include tenant_id
memories.content: In addition to the organization's structured JSON log fields, platform services add tenant_id and request_id to every log entry.

memories.title: Redis for caching
memories.content: Platform services use Redis (ElastiCache) for caching. Memcached is not used.
memories.rationale: Redis also serves rate limiting, so one system is cheaper to run.

memories.title: Kafka for event streaming
memories.content: Platform services publish domain events to Kafka. Topics are named <domain>.<entity>.<event>.v1.

memories.title: Every consumer has a dead-letter topic
memories.content: Kafka consumers route poison messages to a dead-letter topic with the .dlq suffix. An alert fires when a DLQ holds more than 100 messages.

memories.title: Platform services use Go 1.26
memories.content: Platform services moved to go 1.26 in go.mod ahead of the organization schedule to use the new json/v2 package.

memories.title: POST endpoints require an idempotency key
memories.content: Every POST endpoint of payments-api requires the X-Idempotency-Key header. Keys and responses are stored for 24 hours in the idempotency_keys table; a repeated key returns the stored response instead of charging again.

memories.title: Amounts are integer minor units
memories.content: Monetary amounts are stored as bigint minor units (cents) together with an ISO 4217 currency code. Floating point types are never used for money.
memories.rationale: Floating point rounding produced one-cent reconciliation errors.

memories.title: payments-api logs with log/slog
memories.content: payments-api writes JSON logs with the standard library log/slog package instead of zap, keeping third-party dependencies out of the PCI audit scope.

memories.title: payments-api is in PCI DSS scope
memories.content: payments-api is in scope for PCI DSS. Card data is tokenized by the payment processor; the service never stores a primary account number (PAN).

memories.title: Stripe is the primary payment processor
memories.content: Card payments go through Stripe. Adyen is configured as a fallback processor for outages.

memories.title: Refund window is 180 days
memories.content: Customers can request a refund through /v1/refunds for 180 days after the charge. Later refunds need a manual finance approval.

memories.title: payments-api has a dedicated PostgreSQL cluster
memories.content: payments-api runs on its own PostgreSQL cluster rather than the shared platform instance, so maintenance windows and PCI controls can be managed separately.

memories.title: payments-api connection pool
memories.content: payments-api sets DB_POOL_MAX_CONNS=50 per pod because charge bursts exhausted the default pool.

memories.title: Verify Stripe webhook signatures first
memories.content: Verify the Stripe-Signature header and timestamp before parsing a webhook body. In 2025 replayed unsigned webhooks marked refunds as completed.

memories.title: Never retry charge creation without the key
memories.content: A retried charge request without its idempotency key double-charged customers during a processor timeout. Retries of charge creation must reuse the original key.

memories.title: Processor calls time out after 10 seconds
memories.content: Outbound calls to the payment processor use a 10 second timeout and then fail over to the fallback processor.

memories.title: payments-api availability objective
memories.content: payments-api targets 99.95% monthly availability, stricter than the default, because checkout depends on it.

memories.title: payments-api keeps the Jaeger client
memories.content: payments-api continues to use the Jaeger client library for tracing until the PCI re-certification in 2027.

memories.title: Double-entry bookkeeping
memories.content: Every ledger transaction writes balanced debit and credit rows to the ledger_entries table; the sum of a transaction's entries is always zero.

memories.title: Ledger entries are append-only
memories.content: Rows in the ledger are never updated or deleted. A mistake is corrected by posting a reversing entry followed by the correct entry.

memories.title: ledger-service uses CQRS
memories.content: ledger-service separates commands from queries (CQRS). Balance reads come from the ledger_balances_view read model, which a projector updates from Kafka events.

memories.title: Ledger transactions are SERIALIZABLE
memories.content: Ledger writes run at SERIALIZABLE isolation. The service retries transactions that fail with SQLSTATE 40001 serialization_failure up to three times.

memories.title: Balances are not cached
memories.content: ledger-service does not cache account balances in Redis; reads always come from the read model to avoid serving stale balances.

memories.title: ledger-service migrations use Atlas
memories.content: ledger-service manages its schema with Atlas declarative migrations instead of goose, because the ledger schema needs automatic drift detection.

memories.title: New iOS screens use SwiftUI
memories.content: New iOS screens are written in SwiftUI. UIKit is acceptable only when maintaining existing legacy screens.

memories.title: Mobile release train
memories.content: Mobile apps ship on a two-week release train; builds are cut on Tuesdays and submitted to the App Store the same day.

memories.title: Mobile feature flags use Firebase Remote Config
memories.content: Mobile apps read feature flags from Firebase Remote Config, not LaunchDarkly, so flags work offline from the cached config.

memories.title: Mobile analytics through Segment
memories.content: Mobile analytics events are sent through Segment, which forwards them to the warehouse and product tools.

memories.title: ios-app uses The Composable Architecture
memories.content: ios-app structures features with The Composable Architecture (TCA): reducers, stores and dependency clients.

memories.title: Minimum supported iOS version
memories.content: ios-app supports iOS 17 and later; the deployment target was raised in the 4.0 release.

memories.title: Tokens live in the Keychain
memories.content: Access and refresh tokens are stored in the iOS Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock. Never store tokens in UserDefaults.

memories.title: Checkout flow stays in UIKit
memories.content: The ios-app checkout flow remains a UIKit legacy screen until the payment SDK supports SwiftUI.

memories.title: Upload dSYMs in CI
memories.content: Crash reports were unreadable until CI uploaded dSYM files with fastlane upload_symbols_to_crashlytics after each archive.

memories.title: ios-app reads feature flags from LaunchDarkly
memories.content: ios-app uses the LaunchDarkly iOS SDK for feature flags so flags are shared with the web checkout.

memories.title: Snowflake is the data warehouse
memories.content: Analytical data is loaded into Snowflake. BigQuery was considered and rejected because of the EU region requirements.

memories.title: Transformations are dbt models
memories.content: Warehouse transformations are dbt models with schema tests and documentation; ad hoc SQL is not scheduled in production.

memories.title: Change data capture with Debezium
memories.content: Change data capture (CDC) streams PostgreSQL changes through Debezium into Kafka topics consumed by the warehouse loaders.

memories.title: Hash email addresses in analytics
memories.content: Analytics tables never hold raw email addresses; they store SHA-256 hashes with a rotating salt as the pseudonymized identifier.

memories.title: Batch jobs run on Airflow
memories.content: Batch data jobs are orchestrated by Airflow; DAGs live in the analytics-pipeline repository under dags/.

memories.title: Python 3.12 with uv
memories.content: analytics-pipeline targets Python 3.12 and manages dependencies with uv and a committed uv.lock.

memories.title: analytics-pipeline logs with structlog
memories.content: analytics-pipeline is a Python project and logs JSON with structlog, including the trace_id field used by the Go services.

memories.title: Nightly pipeline schedule
memories.content: The nightly analytics-pipeline DAG starts at 02:00 UTC and must finish before 06:00 UTC when dashboards refresh.

memories.title: Raw events kept for 13 months
memories.content: Raw event data is retained for 13 months to allow year-over-year comparisons, then deleted by a scheduled job.

memories.title: analytics-pipeline runs in us-east-1
memories.content: analytics-pipeline processes event data in us-east-1 next to the Snowflake account for lower egress cost.
